processingEvidence.summary: Estimated fees for all practical and studio locations. Calculated practical location fees for 20 shoot days in Africa, including government liaison charges. Calculated studio costs based on a 40-week block booking of 4 large stages at MGM-British Studios to accommodate extensive prep, a 125-day shoot schedule, and wrap. Included costs for ancillary spaces like workshops and offices.

Calculated international and domestic permit costs. For Africa, this includes a national filming permit, animal importation/welfare permits, and customs carnet fees. For the UK, this includes pyrotechnic permits and fees for unprecedented engineering and safety certifications for the large-scale mechanical sets.

Assessed and costed security for both location types. A dedicated security team, secure compound, and crowd control measures were budgeted for the high-risk remote African location. For the studio, costs include 24/7 on-set security, and enhanced access control protocols to protect high-value sets and maintain project confidentiality.

Factored in restoration costs. For Africa, this includes a substantial environmental bond, a dedicated cleanup crew, and oversight from an environmental officer to ensure a 'leave no trace' policy. For the studio, a significant budget was allocated for the strike, removal, and disposal of massive, complex sets.

Calculated costs for essential support facilities. For the remote African shoot, this covers the establishment of a full base camp, including vehicle staging, field kitchens, large-scale power generation with fuel, and water/waste management. For the studio, costs are primarily for the high consumption of electrical power for massive set lighting, plus a contingency for overflow parking.

locationCostSummary.notes: Costs are estimated in 1965-1968 US dollars, reflecting the production era. A significant contingency is included due to the pioneering and unprecedented nature of the production's technical requirements.

confidenceInterval.description: The range reflects the high degree of uncertainty and risk associated with the project's groundbreaking special effects, set construction, and remote international filming in the 1960s.

locationFees.description: Fees for access to national parks/reserves for plains, stream, and cave exterior scenes.

governmentLiaison.description: Mandatory government fixers, park ranger oversight, and local authority coordination.

permits.description: National filming permit, animal welfare/importation permits, and customs carnet.

security.description: On-site security team (10 guards), secure equipment compound, and crowd management.

restorationAndCleanup.description: Environmental bond, 'leave no trace' cleanup crew, and environmental officer.

transportationLogistics.description: International air/sea freight for equipment, plus local rental of 4x4 vehicles.

localSupport.description: Local fixer/liaison services and specialized animal wrangler package for lion and other animals.

studioRental.description: Block booking of 4 large sound stages for 40 weeks to cover prep, shoot, and wrap. Includes office space, workshops, and storage.

permitsAndCertification.description: Permits for on-set pyrotechnics and engineering safety certification for complex mechanical rigs.

security.description: 24/7 on-set security team and enhanced access control for confidential sets.

utilities.description: Metered electrical power consumption for massive set lighting and mechanical rigs.

restorationAndStrike.description: Labor and disposal costs for striking and removing all large-scale sets post-filming.

customSetConstruction.description: Design, engineering, material, and labor costs for constructing groundbreaking and large-scale sets. This was a primary driver of the film's budget.

items.details: 38-foot diameter, 100-ton rotating set with integrated lighting, props, and camera rigging. A major engineering feat.
Large-scale, multi-level set with curved architecture and provisions for a smaller rotating section for docking sequence.
Multiple interconnected sets including conference rooms, airlocks, and a large-scale lunar surface excavation site with complex lighting.
Cockpit and passenger sets for Orion III and Aries-IB spacecraft, designed for zero-gravity effects.
Specialized sets for abstract visual effects sequences and the final Louis XVI-style hotel room.
Studio-built cave set to match practical exteriors, allowing for controlled lighting and effects.

infrastructureDevelopment.description: Costs to establish temporary infrastructure required for filming.

items.details: Establishment of a full base camp: grading for vehicle access, catering tents, field kitchen.
Water and waste management systems, including transport of potable water and disposal of waste.

riskAssessment.description: High risk of delays and cost overruns at the remote African location due to weather, animal availability, and complex logistics for personnel and equipment.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Budget includes a local fixer, contingency days, and an environmental bond. Pre-scouting and establishing strong local contacts is critical.

riskAssessment.description: The unprecedented scale and technical complexity of the studio sets (especially the centrifuge) present a massive risk of engineering challenges, budget overruns, and schedule delays.
riskAssessment.mitigation: A substantial construction budget and a high overall contingency (20%) are allocated. Engaging top-tier engineers and extensive R&D/testing periods are assumed.

riskAssessment.description: Pioneering construction and special effects may face unforeseen regulatory hurdles for safety certification, as standards for such work were not yet established.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Budget allocated for specialized engineering review and certification. Close collaboration with studio safety officers and authorities is required.

riskAssessment.description: Extreme demand for specialized studio space and power. Availability of multiple large stages for an extended period could be a constraint.
riskAssessment.mitigation: Cost estimate is based on a long-term block booking made well in advance. Power costs are budgeted at a premium rate to reflect high consumption.

alternativeLocationOptions.description: Utilize established filming locations in Spanish deserts (e.g., Almería) to replicate African plains. This would significantly reduce logistical complexity, transportation costs, and political risks.
cons: May not have the required wildlife

alternativeLocationOptions.description: Base the entire studio portion of the film in a major Hollywood studio complex instead of the UK.
pros: Access to a large pool of specialized SFX/VFX talent and vendors
Proximity to director and key US-based production staff
cons: Potentially higher union labor costs in the 1960s
Less favorable currency exchange rates at the time
May have required relocating key UK-based department heads (e.g., production design)
